primary_source.title: Boundary Problems for Wave Equations With Grazing and Gliding Rays
locators: Sections 6.1–6.4, normalized Fourier–Airy kernels and the transition/negative-ray decomposition
primary_source.mathematical_scope: Independent mixed derivative estimates, direct distributional construction, finite-loss bound, genuine trace limits and distributional PDE parametrices.

source_correspondence: D0 proves the normal difference, vanishing tangential derivatives at the boundary and one uniform nonstationary tangential direction from the actual mixed Hessian.
D1 proves uniform ordered-line Airy quotient bounds using the full zero-free differentiated Airy asymptotics; exponential factors are retained.

D2 proves every mixed derivative and every normal weight for the transition and positive part. Each purely tangential derivative contributes the normal difference, and exponential decay absorbs all such factors.
D3 removes the negative-ray oscillation exactly and proves all amplitude derivative bounds for both scalar modes with the same complex matrix coefficients.
D4 proves tangential nonstationarity, every reciprocal derivative and the mixed normal/tangential phase-product bound. D5 verifies the transpose sign and a one-third gain per integration by parts.

D6 constructs the operator on every compact distribution through tested absolute convergence, proves all normal derivatives, strong-topology continuity, cutoff independence and uniqueness by common-support approximation.
D7 gives an explicit conservative finite-loss Sobolev bound and continuity in the normal variable. It does not claim the sharp weak energy estimate.
D8 passes the exact value and full complex conormal row to actual boundary limits, proves the smooth PDE residual on singular data and retains the output-cutoff commutator.

D9 composes the actual graph and conormal inverses to obtain distributional Dirichlet and Robin parametrices, including the opposite mode, parameter smoothing errors and represented matching solutions. Completeness for arbitrary weak energy solutions is not inferred.

Three complete exercises check delta-input traces and PDE signs, the failure without tangential nonstationarity and the exact one-third normal-layer gain at fixed frequency. The figure uses the proven Airy combination and exact cutoff coordinates.
Fourteen local nodes connect to 640 earlier entries in 31 maps, including 92 external Lebl providers. Internal export closure, sharp energy mapping and strict propagation remain unclaimed.
